Description

**BIBLE REVIEW** — the Biblical Archaeology Society's magazine of the Bible in history and art — **thirteen issues, October 2002 through the "BR 20 YEARS" anniversary issue**, and **six of them are still inside their original BAS mailing cover wraps.**

What's Included — 13 issues

**2002** — October · December **2003** — February · April · August · October · December **2004** — February · April · June · August · October **Anniversary** — the **"BR 20 YEARS"** issue. Its cover prints *ANNIVERSARY ISSUE · $4.50* with no month. Bible Review launched in 1985, which places a 20-year anniversary issue in **2005** — the magazine's final year, after which it was folded into *Biblical Archaeology Review*. (Stated as the likely year, not a printed one.)

**Please note this is a dense run, not a complete one:** June 2003 and December 2004 are not included, and 2002 is represented by October and December only.

The six original mailing wraps

Six issues arrived still wrapped in the printed outer sheet the Society mailed around each copy, and they are still wrapped. These usually went straight in the bin, so they rarely survive:

  • Two **"Gift Subscriptions"** wraps (red and orange) and one in purple.
  • Two **"Travel & Learn"** wraps carrying the **2003** BAS Travel/Study schedule — Oxford (August 3–15), Churches of Revelation & Acts in Greece & Turkey with Jim Fleming (October 17–26), and seminars in Los Angeles, Chicago, Phoenix/Scottsdale and Atlanta (Fest VI).
  • One **"Tour de Force"** wrap carrying the **2004** schedule — Eastern Turkey and Discover Egypt with Avner Goren, Bible Fest VII in San Antonio, plus St. Olaf, Reed and Wake Forest summer seminars.

Condition

Very Good.

  • Covers bright and glossy, colors strong. Spines flat and tight on all thirteen.
  • **No writing on any magazine.**
  • Light edge or corner wear and a soft edge crease on four issues (Dec 2003, Apr 2004, Jun 2004, and the anniversary issue) — cosmetic, nothing through the cover art.
  • The wraps show ordinary mail handling — soft corners, light curl. None torn away.
  • **One handwritten mark in the whole lot:** a date, "10/8/2004," in black ink across the top of one purple *Gift Subscriptions* wrap. It is shown in the photos.
  • **Mailing labels:** the original subscriber address labels are still attached — on the wrap for the wrapped copies, on the cover for the rest. They are adhered to the paper, so they have been left in place rather than risk a tear. For the previous owner's privacy, the printed name and address are **covered with a plain gray block in the listing photos**; the magazines and wraps you receive still carry the original labels, exactly as pictured apart from that block.
  • Interiors were not photographed. Nothing at the block edge indicates torn-out or missing pages, but page-by-page completeness is not claimed.

About this item

Bible Review was the art-historical half of the Biblical Archaeology Society's output — every cover a fine-art reproduction, and these thirteen are a good run of them: Caravaggio's *Crucifixion of St Peter*, Cranach's *Samson and Delilah*, a Tiepolo ceiling tondo, an early Christian catacomb orant, Raphael's *Holy Family with the Lamb*, and Book of Hours miniatures. The magazine stopped publishing in 2005, so the anniversary issue closes out the title.

All thirteen issues and all six wraps ship together in one package.
